The four parts: dendrites, soma, axon, terminal buttons, each with a one-line job and an analogy with limits
The electrochemical signal idea: electrical within the neuron, chemical between neurons
The synapse as the small gap between neurons where the chemical step occurs
The all-or-none principle, stated simply with an original example
Myelin as the insulation that speeds signals
The honest framing: neurons are the wires, and the mind is what the wiring does

claims.claim: Neurons are the specialized cells of the nervous system that carry information; OpenStax describes them as the central building blocks of the nervous system, roughly 100 billion strong at birth, and as interconnected information processors essential for all of the tasks of the nervous system.

A neuron's dendrites are branching extensions that serve as input sites where signals are received from other neurons; the soma (cell body) holds the nucleus; the axon is the major extension that carries the signal electrically away from the soma; the axon ends in multiple terminal buttons.

Neuronal communication is an electrochemical event: the movement of the action potential down the axon is an electrical event, and the movement of the neurotransmitter across the synaptic space is the chemical portion of the process.

The synapse is the very small space between neurons and is an important site where communication between neurons occurs; the axon of one neuron typically comes into close contact with the dendrite of another at a synapse.

The action potential is an all-or-none phenomenon: an incoming signal is either sufficient or insufficient to reach the threshold of excitation, with no in-between, and there is no turning off an action potential once it starts.
In many axons, glial cells form a fatty substance called the myelin sheath, which coats the axon and acts as an insulator, increasing the speed at which the signal travels.

Psychologists study the nervous system because learning how the body's cells and organs function can help us understand the biological basis of human psychology (OpenStax); this grounds the interpretive framing that neurons are the wiring and the mind is what the wiring does.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether neurons or glial cells are more numerous in the human brain
positions: Long-standing teaching held that glial cells outnumber neurons by roughly 10 to 1
Recent work from Suzanna Herculano-Houzel's laboratory has called that assumption into question, with evidence suggesting a nearly 1:1 ratio (OpenStax)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson makes no claim about relative numbers; it mentions glial cells only in their well-supported supportive role.
